title: Physical laws govern the whole configuration of later-stage segmenting eggs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Physical laws govern the whole configuration of later-stage segmenting eggs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The whole configuration of an egg in advanced stages of segmentation is determined by simple physical laws just as in the two- and four-celled stages, even though the mathematics becomes too difficult to follow.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We have little reason to doubt, and no just cause to disbelieve, that the whole configuration, for instance of an egg in the advanced stages of segmentation, is accurately determined by simple physical laws

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Physical laws in advanced segmentation”. Scope: segmenting eggs of animals at all cleavage stages

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-14: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Abundant embryo datasets exist, but the claim does not state a model whose predictions could fail. Without specifying the 'simple physical laws,' observed configurations cannot discriminate this assertion from its rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A test would require a specified set of physical laws that predicts complete later embryo geometry before comparison with 4D developmental images.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Any material configuration is in some sense governed by physical laws.

No particular laws, parameters, or error criterion are stated.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Late-cleavage images are public and can be checked against the Plateau-type constraints developed for early stages, which is a fair partial reading of the claim. The assertion that the whole configuration is accurately determined by simple physical laws does not name which laws, and many outcomes fit both those laws and lineage-specific developmental programs. Only the restricted geometric continuation is testable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Ask whether late-cleavage geometry continues to satisfy the same minimal-surface and contact rules that fix the two- and four-cell stages, with no extra lineage-specific parameters. Late embryos whose contacts and angles match a surface-mechanics extrapolation would support that reading; stereotyped positions that violate those constraints would limit it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simple physical laws can be stretched to cover almost any material configuration, so the decision rule needs a pre-specified constraint set.

Fitting a full mechanical model of advanced cleavage is specialist work and is longer than a routine remeasurement.
